terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: Static single-storey branded retail box on thaikit's shared 8.0 x 4.6 x 7.0 m module, exterior shell only. No interior geometry: glazing is a tinted mostly-opaque pane, not an opening. Nothing moves, so one root pivot and zero sockets is the correct contract. Distinguishing features on this plate: cream render walls, a deep PURPLE fascia band with SCB in white and the gold leaf mark, a purple entrance surround and a purple ATM surround carrying TWO ATMs, a stepped stone plinth projecting forward at the base, a grey double service door and two barred windows on the +X wall, a pale coping ring at one level all the way round, and four louvred rooftop units standing above it. No entrance canopy.

reasoning: Silhouette is a single rectangular prism -- low geometric complexity.
Richness is REPETITION and PANELLING, not intricate form. The instanced systems collapse the repeated parts into one InstancedMesh each.
Occlusion risk is real: the rear elevation is entirely unseen in the single plate.
Action readiness is minimal: static exterior shell, box collider, not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Repetition-dominated facade: without repetitionSystems the mullion and plant sets would each cost a draw call per part and blow maxDrawCalls=12.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

details.description: white SCB wordmark beside a gold leaf mark on the purple band
deep purple fascia band across the whole front
purple ATM surround standing proud of the facade, with two niches recessed 0.25 m into it
two stainless ATM kiosks in the niches, each with a curved front carrying the kiosk-face image
frameless double glass door in a purple portal, with stile, patch rails and paired pull bars, glass above the header and a transom rail across the whole glass wall
stepped stone plinth projecting forward at the base
hooded double service door with a handle and two hooded barred windows behind it on the +X wall, at the rectified positions
four louvred galvanised rooftop units with fan guards standing above the coping
pale coping ring 2 cm proud on every parapet face, one level all the way round
plate glass reads as a tight specular lobe, unlike every other surface

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

resolvedUnknowns: Rear (-Z) and left (-X) elevations are unobserved; authored plain. Confidence 0.20 / 0.25.

The plate's glazing is transparent over a lit banking hall. Not modelled: this is an exterior shell, and on the brief (fourth build) the pane carries NO interior image -- the projected view of the third build had no parallax and slid against the portal and the framing as the camera moved. It is plain tinted plate glass, #4b5c60 at opacity 0.90, over a dark backdrop slab folded into the roof-deck submission by vertex tone. Rendered at azimuth 0 it measures luma 66 against the plate pane's 66, held out of the silhouette gate by saturation (0.29 rendered, gate threshold 0.16) rather than by lifting it to grey.

The two ATMs are stainless kiosks in RECESSED niches with a CURVED front (bulge 0.07 m) that carries a frontal kiosk-face image -- screen, keypad, card and cash slots -- generated by Nano Banana 2 from the plate's own ATM crop. The curved fronts ride the fascia material and sample the right-hand strip of the same atlas as the sign, so they cost no draw call and no material.
The sign is BAKED (sign/compose2.py): the wordmark and the bo-leaf are Nano Banana 2 edits of the plate's sign crop, laid out at the plate ratios in a 2048 x 1024 atlas (16 KB WebP).

The glazing is ONE continuous glass wall (x -3.50..1.10) with a light stainless perimeter frame, a transom rail at 2.21 m and one dark mullion; the two door leaves stand proud of it in the same submission, and the two barred windows on +X are panes in the same component.

The +X elevation is homography-rectified off the plate (wall corners 655,357 / 955,293 / 937,638 / 655,753 -> z +-3.5, y 0..4.6): service door z 0.03..1.45 x y 0.09..2.56 with a pale hood over it; barred windows z -1.45..-0.52 and -2.90..-2.03 at y 2.35..3.15, BEHIND the door, each with a hood, a light frame, four vertical and one horizontal dark bar and a dark pane. The third build had the windows in front of the door and the door 1 m too far back.

The coping is ONE continuous ring at one level (rectified y 4.30..4.60), 2 cm proud of every parapet face, in the wall render: the plate shows it a shade lighter than the wall (#e2d4b7 against #cec1a7). The third build stopped the side upstands 0.65 m below the front.

The rooftop units are louvred packaged units: casing under a flanged lid with a fan disc on top, a round fan guard on the front, a nine-blade louvre on one end, panel seams, feet -- one instanced geometry with per-part vertex tones, on the roof-deck MATERIAL so the plant and the membrane share a galvanised spangle tile (baked for the Flash Express plant) without a ninth material; the membrane keeps its own tone (deckTone). Deck raised to 4.09..4.21 inside the ring so the units stand above the coping as the plate's do: their tops reach 4.965, an 8% overrun on one axis inside the asset's 10% tolerance, with walls, parapet and coping at 4.60.

The door is two frameless glass leaves (opening 1.36 x 1.75 m) with a meeting stile, bottom patch rails, a closer strip and paired pull bars, in a purple portal whose header sits at the transom line with glass above it. FIXED geometry -- no pivot; nothing on this prop opens.
preSpecAssessment.unknownsResolutionNote: Emptied because every entry has been RESOLVED with a recorded authoring decision, not because the gaps went away. Each is restated in assumptions and in viewEvidence with its confidence and a null path. Nothing was invented to close a gap.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 8.0 x 4.6 x 7.0 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=16000 triangles, <=12 draw calls, <=8 materials, <=16 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot and zero sockets; box collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

pivotInventory.name: root
pivotInventory.justification: The ONLY mechanism this prop has. Nothing opens, turns or swings; doors and shutters are authored as fixed geometry, so they get no axis. A named pivot is a promise that a part turns on it.

actionReadiness.socketJustification: ZERO sockets, deliberately. Nothing attaches to this prop and nothing is emitted from it. A marker named for a place on the surface is a location, not a mechanism.

colliderInventory.note: The asset declares collider 'box'. One box proxy.

actionReadiness.destructionJustification: The asset declares destructionGroups as an empty list -- this prop is NOT breakable. No component carries actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup. promote-model checks built against declared as an equality in BOTH directions, so an invented group fails the gate just as a missing one would.

coordinateFrame.notes: Origin base-center as the asset declares. The shopfront faces +Z. Glazing sits LEFT of the entrance and the ATM surround RIGHT of it, so the facade is strongly asymmetric about X; the service door and barred windows are on +X only. No mirror plane is declared.

silhouette.description: One rectangular prism. The silhouette events are the stone plinth stepping forward at the base, the purple ATM surround standing proud of the facade, the coping ring, and four rooftop units breaking the roofline above it. No cantilever.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: x spans -4.00..+4.00 (parapet ring outer faces) = 8.00. y spans 0.00..4.60 = 4.60. z spans -3.50 (rear parapet) ..+3.50 = 7.00. The shell front face is set back to z=+2.50 so anything cantilevering off it lands ON the declared depth rather than overrunning it.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate normalises to w:h:d = 1 : 0.572 : 0.915 against the declared 1 : 0.575 : 0.875 -- height agrees to 0.6%, the closest agreement in the whole retail set, and depth reads 4.5% deeper. The declared module is corroborated here rather than merely asserted.

viewEvidence.note: NOT OBSERVED. Authored as plain render with the parapet returning and no openings.
NOT OBSERVED. Authored plain; the service door and barred windows are NOT mirrored.

componentTree.name: Building shell
componentTree.topologyRationale: One continuous render skin over four walls. Splitting it per elevation would cost a draw call per wall for the life of the prop to express one material.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Solid box, x -3.94..+3.94, y 0..3.55, z -3.44..+2.50. SOLID, not a ring: the prop is an exterior shell only ever seen from outside, so an interior would cost draw calls, geometries and VRAM for something nobody sees. Solid also means the shopfront needs no opening cut in it, which removes all four reveal faces and the z-fighting they cause.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Set 0.06 m INSIDE the parapet ring on every elevation (walls at +-3.94 and -3.44; parapet at +-4.00 and -3.50). That difference is a coping drip edge, and it is what stops a wall face and a parapet face being coplanar and co-facing.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Flat painted cement render, roughness 0.88, no texture set.

pivot.name: root
pivot.notes: base-center, as the asset declares. A STATIC exterior shell: nothing opens, turns or swings, so one root pivot is the whole mechanism inventory and that is the correct answer, not a gap.

collider.notes: Declared on the asset as box. One convex proxy over the whole envelope; a level builder collides with the building, not with its canopy plates.

componentTree.name: Roof deck
componentTree.topologyRationale: A flat deck plane. Its own component only because the membrane is a visibly different value from the wall render, and this prop is seen from above in every hero shot.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Thin slab spanning y 3.50..3.62, overlapping UNDER the parapet ring.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Spans y 3.50..3.62 so its underside is sunk INTO the shell rather than resting on it. Authored flush, the deck bottom face and the parapet ring bottom face would both sit at y=3.550 facing down -- tens of square metres of coplanar co-facing surface, and exactly the pair check-coplanar catches.

localFeatures.description: four louvred rooftop units with fan guards

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Galvanised material, vertex-toned: the membrane at 0xe6dfd3 (renders 179 against the plate membrane's 197) and, in the same submission, the dark backdrop slab 4 mm off the shell face behind the whole glass wall (0x484848) that the plain tinted pane looks into. Deck raised to 4.09..4.21 inside the parapet ring.

actionProfile.notes: Rigidly parented to the root. NO pivot and NO socket, deliberately: this part does not move and nothing attaches to it.

componentTree.name: Parapet ring and fascia wall
componentTree.topologyRationale: A continuous upstand ring in one material, with the front simply taller -- which a plan extrusion cannot express, since an extrude carries one height. Merged boxes are the right primitive, and anything else in the same material folds in here rather than costing its own submission.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Front fascia wall plus left, right and rear upstands, merged into ONE component and ONE draw call, with same-material cladding folded in.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Parapet outer faces stand 0.06 m PROUD of the shell walls. Authored flush they would be coplanar and co-facing along all three elevations. The front box overlaps into the shell volume rather than butting it.
geometryDescriptor.mergeNote: Primitive is "box" because the schema enumerates primitives, but this is a MERGED cluster built into one BufferGeometry and submitted as ONE draw call.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: The SAME cream render as the shell -- one material. A 0.94 m ring at ONE level on all four faces under a coping 2 cm proud of each, plus the pale hoods over the +X door and windows, all folded into this submission.

actionProfile.notes: Rigidly parented to the root. NO pivot and NO socket, deliberately: this part does not move and nothing attaches to it.

componentTree.name: Brand fascia panel
componentTree.topologyRationale: A flat panel carrying the brand mark. UV strategy is AUTHORED, not generated: the +Z face samples the wordmark region of the canvas and the other five faces sample a plain corner of the same canvas. That is what keeps the brand graphic at one material and one draw call instead of adding a separate graphic plane.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Brand fascia panel, sunk INTO the fascia wall at the back and standing proud of it at the front, so it overlaps its surround instead of meeting it.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Back face is inside the fascia wall solid and the front face clears every other facade plane. No coincident face anywhere on this panel.

localFeatures.description: SCB and the gold leaf mark

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Purple sign panel, roughness 0.40. A separate material from the identical band ONLY because it carries the baked atlas -- the sign band AND the two curved kiosk faces, merged into this component so both textured surfaces are one submission.

actionProfile.notes: Rigidly parented to the root. NO pivot and NO socket, deliberately: this part does not move and nothing attaches to it.

componentTree.name: Shopfront glazing
componentTree.topologyRationale: One pane, not one per bay: the mullion grid in front does the dividing, and a pane per bay would cost a draw call each to express one sheet of glass.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Single tinted pane, overlapping INTO the facade at the back and RECESSED behind the framing at the front, which is what makes it read as glass set into a frame.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Front face sits behind the frame and mullion fronts; back face is inside the facade solid. No coincident face.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Plain dark tinted pane, roughness 0.12, opacity 0.90, NO interior image. ONE pane for the whole glass wall (x -3.50..1.10) plus the two door leaves proud of it and the two barred windows' panes on +X (glazingExtra) -- one material, one submission. The dark room behind it is the roof-deck's backdrop slab; the purple portal and the light frame in front do the dividing.

actionProfile.notes: Rigidly parented to the root. NO pivot and NO socket, deliberately: this part does not move and nothing attaches to it.

componentTree.name: Shopfront framing and door bay
componentTree.topologyRationale: Every one of these parts is the same metal. Folding them into one component is the draw-call lever chosen in the BLOCKOUT -- a part split for authoring convenience cannot be merged afterwards once pivots hang off it.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Perimeter frame, transom, kick rail, door jambs and door header MERGED into one component.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Frame front face stands proud of both the glazing and the mullions. The frame OVERLAPS the glazing it holds rather than meeting its edge, which is the rule that stops a frame putting four coincident reveal faces in the model.
geometryDescriptor.mergeNote: Merged multi-box cluster, one BufferGeometry, one draw call.

localFeatures.description: door stile, patch rails and closer strip
tight specular lobe on the pane it frames

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Near-black powder-coated steel, metalness 0.25. Carries the door's stile, patch rails and closer strip, the ATM niche trims, and on +X the dark reveals behind the service door and the windows, the window bars and the door's meeting gap, in one submission; the perimeter frame is the LIGHT stainless, as the plate shows.

actionProfile.notes: Rigidly parented to the root. NO pivot and NO socket, deliberately: this part does not move and nothing attaches to it.

componentTree.name: Metal fittings: glazing frame, door pulls, ATM kiosks, service door and window frames
componentTree.topologyRationale: Every stainless fitting shares one material. Grouping by MATERIAL rather than by location is what keeps them at one draw call; grouped by elevation they would have been three.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: The light perimeter frame, sill, head and transom rail of the glass wall, the two kiosk bodies behind their curved fronts, the paired door pull bars, and on the +X wall the two service-door leaves with a lever handle and the frames of the two barred windows, at the positions the rectified elevation gives.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: +X depth bands from the shell face at 3.94: dark reveals 3.940..3.965, panes 3.945..3.965, bars 3.965..3.985, leaves and frames 3.965..3.995, the parapet face at 4.00, the coping 4.02, the hoods 4.05 -- every component's outermost +X plane its own. The kiosk body front is at 3.38, 2 cm behind the surround face at 3.40; the head rail tops at 3.13 and the pane 1 cm under it.

localFeatures.description: two ATM kiosks in recessed niches

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Brushed stainless / grey steel, metalness 0.35. One component for every metal fitting on the prop wherever it sits -- the glazing frame and transom rail, the two kiosk bodies, the door pull bars, and on +X the service door's two leaves and lever handle and the two window frames.

actionProfile.notes: Rigidly parented to the root. NO pivot and NO socket, deliberately: this part does not move and nothing attaches to it.

componentTree.name: Purple fascia band, entrance portal and ATM surround
componentTree.topologyRationale: Five boxes in one cladding material. Separately they would cost five submissions to express one system.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Purple band across the front, an entrance portal standing in the glass wall with its header at the transom line, and a proud ATM surround carved into two niches by piers, a top rail and a back panel.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: The band is 7.92 m wide against a 7.88 m shell so its side faces clear the wall planes. The recess reaches x=3.96, not 4.00: at 2.90 m wide it ran out to exactly the parapet's own outer plane.

localFeatures.description: ATM surround with two recessed niches

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Purple panelled cladding, roughness 0.45. Band, entrance surround and ATM surround are one material and therefore one component and one draw call.

actionProfile.notes: Rigidly parented to the root. NO pivot and NO socket, deliberately: this part does not move and nothing attaches to it.

componentTree.name: Stone plinth
componentTree.topologyRationale: Two stepped runs in one material.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Stepped plinth projecting forward of the facade at the base.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Projects to z=3.50 exactly -- the declared envelope face. Authored 0.40 m deeper it pushed the prop to 7.5 m against a declared 7.0.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Cast-stone plinth, roughness 0.60, under a terrazzo speckle tile. Two steps, one material, one draw call.

actionProfile.notes: Rigidly parented to the root. NO pivot and NO socket, deliberately: this part does not move and nothing attaches to it.

roughness.notes: Scalar observed for this surface in the plate. The independently extracted map is kept on disk as evidence and is NOT bound at runtime -- this material is textureless, so the scalar is the runtime value.

albedo.samplingNotes: Measured as the mean of crops/wall.png. extract_pbr_evidence confidence 0.756. The extractor palette is advisory only: these crops are flat material swatches, not isolated objects, so its foreground separation is weak by its own warnings. Albedo is the direct crop measurement.

evidence: Measured on viewEvidence region-wall (PBR confidence 0.756): flat painted render with no high-frequency component at plate resolution. Plate side wall #cec1a7 (luma 195); authored #d8c9ae rendered 154 on the hero side wall under the harness and the render tile only darkens, so the albedo is lifted toward the plate reading (renders 161).

acceptance: Silhouette reads correctly without materials.
Quality contract has named all required macro feature groups before code generation.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Build the component hierarchy implied by the pre-spec complexity assessment.
acceptance: Macro, meso, and repeated structures meet qualityContract.minimumSpecDepth.
Parent-child relations, joints, seams, sockets, and contact points are explicit.
Every attached child appendage/connector has parentSocket, localStart/localEnd, contactType, embedDepth or overlap, and gapTolerance.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Refine shape, deformation, bevels, tapers, curves, asymmetry, and visible local geometry.
acceptance: Important visible forms are represented in component geometryDescriptor, deformations, localFeatures, or repetitionSystems.
Endpoint-based child parts are rooted at their attachment sockets and do not visibly float away from parents.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Match material color, roughness, bump, and local variation.
acceptance: Reference-derived albedo palette records dominant, secondary, and accent colors per visible material.
Each important material defines roughness variation and at least one normal/bump/displacement response.
Local material overrides, dirt/wear/stains/moss/chips/scratches or equivalent masks are tied to evidenceRefs.
Thin, transparent, reflective, wet, or fibrous materials document alpha/transmission/clearcoat/metalness/fiber response when relevant.
Generated preview uses procedural albedo/roughness/bump texture or vertex color variation instead of one flat color.
Generated preview uses independent PBR maps at 1024px or higher for the quality-first tier.
If source pixels are available, referencePbr extraction passed at confidence >= 0.7 or the pass is stopped/requesting better references.
Macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands are visible at the intended review distance without obvious tiling.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Add procedural surface locality such as normal/bump/displacement, AO, dirt, stains, chips, grain, moss, scratches, and wear.
acceptance: Every required material feature group has local overrides or surfaceDetail tied to evidenceRefs.
A grazing-angle close-up proves that normal/height detail breaks highlights naturally and does not read as smooth plastic.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Make material and form readable under neutral turntable lighting plus optional reference lighting.
acceptance: lightingFromPhoto identifies key light direction/color/intensity, fill light, rim or environment light, and ambient color.
Exposure, tone mapping, background color/gradient, shadow softness, and contact shadow behavior are specified.
Lighting does not hide geometry/material gaps and screenshots can be compared fairly to the reference.
Neutral, grazing, and reference-matched lighting checks distinguish material errors from lighting errors.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Make the model ready for future animation, transformation, physics, or destruction.
acceptance: Macro and movable meso components have stable pivot nodes.
Sockets, collider proxies, and destruction metadata are present for future runtime actions.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Protect runtime performance after visual fidelity is accepted.
acceptance: Triangle count, draw calls, instancing, LOD strategy, and FPS target are documented or verified.
Repeated detail is instanced or simplified where possible without breaking silhouette/material believability.

reviewHistory.summary: Material pass: 8 materials, all textureless in the spec. The glazing is plain tinted plate (#4b5c60, renders luma 66 = the plate pane) over a dark vertex-toned backdrop slab -- the projected interior view is gone on the brief. The plant rides the deck material (galvanised, vertex-toned membrane and slab) so it can carry the baked spangle tile without a ninth material. Two atlases: the sign/kiosk atlas on the fascia and the galv tile on the deck; two drawn canvases: a faint render tile on the walls and a terrazzo tile on the plinth.

Surface pass: render drift and streaks on the walls (patchAmp 8 / streakAmp 9 at 3.2 m), terrazzo speckle on the plinth, galvanised spangle on the plant and membrane, per-part tones on the units. The coping and the purple stay clean, as the plate shows them.

Lighting pass: near-shadowless studio plate, so measured crop means stand as albedo. Wall albedo lifted to #e4d6bb because the harness renders a side face at ~0.76 of the authored value and the tile only darkens (renders 161 against the plate's 195). Exposure 1.0, ACES filmic.
Interaction pass: ONE pivot (root, base-center), ZERO sockets, one box collider matching the declaration, no destruction groups matching the empty declared list.

reviewHistory.summary: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.92, up from 0.87. 3076/16000 triangles, 11/12 draw calls, 8/12 materials, 11/16 unique geometries. Draw calls remain the binding axis. The brief's item is on the model: plain tinted glass with no interior image. Residuals: the purple renders a shade darker than the plate, the plinth a shade lighter, the four units share one geometry where the plate has three shapes, and the plate's lit interior is by rule not shown.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the hero2x class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: Two repetition systems collapse 6 parts into 2 submissions; five purple boxes fold into one component and five stainless fittings into another -- grouped by MATERIAL rather than by elevation, which is what keeps the ATMs and the +X door in the same submission.

materials.note: Eight of eight materials, at the material ceiling. wall covers shell, parapet, coping and hoods; purple covers band, surround and recess; metal covers both ATMs, the frame rails, the service door and the window frames; deck covers the membrane, the backdrop slab AND all four rooftop units by vertex tone. fascia duplicates purple ONLY because it carries the wordmark canvas.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: Triangles are NOT the binding constraint on this prop -- draw calls are. The headroom is deliberately spent on silhouette quality (chamfers, cowl segments, shutter ribs) and must not be read as room to split components, which would spend the axis that is actually scarce.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: box, cylinder and merged-box clusters only. No organic surfaces exist on this subject.
Two InstancedMesh systems carry 5 of the 30 discrete parts.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.

Every material is declared textureless. The brand fascia receives its wordmark as a generated canvas assigned AFTER material construction -- the documented route for a printed brand fascia, unaffected by the declaration.

risks.description: Rear and left elevations are not in the single plate; authored plain.
The plain pane renders at luma 66, eight levels above the backdrop; it is chroma (0.29 rendered) that keeps it out of the silhouette gate.
risks.mitigation: Turntable gate run at all four azimuths without --allow-holes; saturation authored at 0.22 and measured on the render.
Any further refinement must reuse an existing material or merge two; the sharing is documented per material so a future editor can see what is already doubled up.
